etymologies.etymologyHTML: 1398, “making,” from Old French, from Latin efficientem, nominative efficiēns, participle of efficere (“work out, accomplish”) (see effect). Meaning “productive, skilled” is from 1787. Efficiency apartment is first recorded 1930, American English.

definitions.definition: making good, thorough, or careful use of resources; not consuming extra. Especially, making good use of time or energy

quote.citation: 2013 June 1, “A better waterworks”, in The Economist‎[1], volume 407, number 8838, page 5 (Technology Quarterly):
quote.text: An artificial kidney these days still means a refrigerator-sized dialysis machine. Such devices mimic […] real kidneys […] . But they are nothing like as efficient, and can cause bleeding, clotting and infection—not to mention inconvenience for patients, who typically need to be hooked up to one three times a week for hours at a time.

Our cleaners are almost too efficient: they throw away anything left out on a desk.

definitions.definition: expressing the proportion of consumed energy that was successfully used in a process; the ratio of useful output to total input
causing effects, producing results; bringing into being; initiating change (rare except in philosophical and legal expression efficient cause = causative factor or agent)

quote.citation: 1614, Walter Ralegh [i.e., Walter Raleigh], The Historie of the World […], London:  […]  William Stansby for Walter Burre, […], →OCLC, (please specify |book=1 to 5):
quote.text: It was well said of Plotinus, that the stars were significant, but not efficient.

quote.citation: 1801, Robert Southey, “(please specify the page)”, in Thalaba the Destroyer, volume (please specify |volume=I or II), London:  […]  [F]or T[homas] N[orton] Longman and O[wen] Rees, […], by Biggs and Cottle, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: Ye wake no more to anguish;‥ ye have borneThe Chosen, the Destroyer!‥ soon his handShall strike the efficient blow;Soon shaking off your penal forms, shall ye,With songs of joy, amid the Eden groves,Hymn the Deliverer’s praise!

quote.citation: 1856, William Dexter Wilson, An Elementary Treatise on Logic:
quote.text: The Efficient Cause is that from which emanates the force that produces the Effect

definitions.definition: (obsolete) a cause; something that causes an effect

quote.text: Some are without efficient, as God; others without matter, as Angels […].

quote.citation: a. 1758, Jonathan Edwards, Dissertation on Liberty and Necessity:
quote.text: This implies, that something happens without a cause. If it should be said, that motive in this case is not the efficient of the action or doing — this is granted; but at the same time, for reasons already given, it is denied, that the man himself is the efficient cause of it.
